I've found two bugs in the Excalidraw codebase that need to be fixed.

*   AnimationController.start(key, callback) must invoke the callback synchronously on the first frame immediately upon being called.

*   When the callback passed to AnimationController.start returns { keep: true }, the animation continues and the next frame is scheduled.

*   When the callback passed to AnimationController.start returns null, the animation stops and the key is removed from the set of running animations.

*   AnimationController.running(key) must return false after an animation associated with that key has naturally ended (callback returned null) or been cancelled.

*   AnimationController.cancel(key) must stop a running animation; after cancellation a new animation can be successfully started with a different key.

*   When all animations have stopped or been cancelled and no frames are pending, there must be no remaining scheduled timers.

*   When updateScene is called with a collaborators map containing an entry whose pointer has tool set to 'laser' and button set to 'down', a path element must appear in the SVG layer of the canvas.

*   When updateScene is called with an empty collaborators map (all collaborators removed), all laser trail path elements previously rendered for remote collaborators must be removed from the SVG layer.


*   Interface details: Type: Class
Name: AnimationController
Location: packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts
Description: Static class that manages multiple named animations. Provides methods to start, cancel, and query animations by string key. Each animation runs frame by frame via a callback that controls continuation.
Signature:
  static start(key: string, callback: (frame: { state: any }) => { keep: true } | null): void
  static cancel(key: string): void
  static running(key: string): boolean


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the relevant files to understand the codebase.

Both fixes are complete, typecheck passes, and existing laser tests pass. Here's a summary of what I changed:

## Bug 1: `AnimationController` (`packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts`)

The controller tracked a boolean `isRunning` flag but **never stored the scheduled timer/RAF handle**. This caused two failures:

- **`cancel()` left a stale timer scheduled.** Deleting the animation from the map didn't clear the pending `setTimeout`/`requestAnimationFrame`, and `isRunning` was never reset to `false` — so after cancelling the last animation there was still a timer pending (violating "no remaining scheduled timers"), and a subsequent `start()` with a new key wouldn't schedule its own frame because `isRunning` was stuck `true`.
- The old `tick()` also short-circuited oddly on completion.

Fixes:
- Store the pending frame in `frameHandle` (with `frameUsesRAF` to know whether to `clearTimeout` vs `cancelAnimationFrame`).
- `cancelFrame()` clears the pending frame and resets the handle when the animation set becomes empty — both in `cancel()` and when a callback returns `null` on the synchronous first frame.
- `scheduleFrame()` is idempotent (guards on `frameHandle !== null`), replacing the fragile `isRunning` flag.
- `tick()` clears the handle up front, runs each callback (deleting keys that return `null`), and reschedules only if animations remain.

The synchronous first-frame invocation and the generic state-based callback contract (used by `InteractiveCanvas`) are preserved; `{ keep: true }` (truthy) continues, `null` stops.

## Bug 2: laser trails (`packages/excalidraw/laser-trails.ts`)

`updateCollabTrails()` early-returned when `collaborators.size === 0`, which **skipped the cleanup loop** that removes trails for departed collaborators. So when `updateScene` was called with an empty collaborators map, previously-rendered remote laser trail `<path>` elements were never removed. Changed the guard to only bail on a missing `container`, so the cleanup loop (which stops and detaches trails no longer present in `collaborators`) always runs.
